hints: Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ separately to the trailer and to the car.
For the trailer, the forward tension is $300\text{ N}$ and resistance is $200\text{ N}$, so $300 - 200 = 1.25m$.
For the car, driving force is $3200\text{ N}$, backwards tension is $300\text{ N}$, and resistance is $F$, so $3200 - F - 300 = 1500(1.25)$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the trailer to find its mass $m$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} = ma$$
$$300 - 200 = 1.25m$$
$$100 = 1.25m \implies m = \frac{100}{1.25} = 80\text{ kg}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the car to find the resistance force $F$:
$$D - F - T = m_{\text{car}}a$$
$$3200 - F - 300 = 1500(1.25)$$
$$2900 - F = 1875 \implies F = 2900 - 1875 = 1025\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ to the trailer. The horizontal forces acting on the trailer are the forward tension $T = 300\text{ N}$ and the opposing resistance of $200\text{ N}$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} = ma$$
$$300 - 200 = m(1.25)$$
$$100 = 1.25m$$

Divide both sides by $1.25$ to solve for mass $m$:
$$m = \frac{100}{1.25} = 80\text{ kg}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the towing car of mass $1500\text{ kg}$. The forward driving force is $3200\text{ N}$, opposed by the backward tension $T = 300\text{ N}$ and resistance $F$:
$$D - T - F = m_{\text{car}} a$$
$$3200 - 300 - F = (1500)(1.25)$$
$$2900 - F = 1875$$
